review_scope: Full 64-line article read. Roles and SAML/SCIM conditions retained; linked identity-provider guidance, second reusable and actual target permissions remain unresolved. No membership or credential mutation authorized.

claims.statement: Enterprise owners are the documented actors for managing their own role in an organization owned by the enterprise.
The article declares ghec and ghes applicability, not general free-plan applicability.
The article distinguishes joining as a member, joining as an owner, changing one's role and leaving an enterprise-owned organization.
An enterprise owner without an organization role cannot access its content or repositories in the documented role model.
An unaffiliated enterprise owner can still manage enterprise settings and policies affecting the organization; that authority is distinct from repository-content access.
Organization membership gives documented access to resources and content but not organization settings; actual repository access must still be read back for the target.
Organization ownership includes configuring organization settings and managing resource access through teams in the article.
The ghec-only warning says joining a SCIM-provisioned organization through role-management settings may have unintended consequences.
Enterprise settings provide the documented general route for joining and managing one's organization role, subject to the article's SAML exception.
For ghec organizations enforcing SAML SSO, joining must occur through the organization's IdP rather than enterprise settings.
The enterprise UI exposes distinct join-as-owner and join-as-member actions; navigating to them does not authorize a privilege change.
The SAML-specific section repeats the IdP joining requirement.
The SAML joining procedure requires IdP assignment to the organization's cloud application and refers unresolved configuration access to an IdP administrator.
The SAML joining procedure requires authentication to the organization with SAML SSO.
The SCIM branch directs acceptance of the invitation generated by the SCIM integration.
The non-SCIM branch directs organization-specific SSO authentication rather than substituting an invented organization or identity.
After joining under the ghec SAML procedure, enterprise settings can manage the organization role, including becoming an owner; this is documented capability, not approved escalation.
